donnees.titre: Autophagy in ocular health and disease: From mechanistic insights to therapeutic perspectives.
donnees.resume: Autophagy represents a lysosomal degradative pathway through which cells systematically break down and recycle their own constituents, including proteins, lipid droplets, and entire organelles, by sequestering them within double-membrane autophagosomes prior to lysosomal fusion. Beyond its role as a fundamental quality control mechanism, this process critically shapes cellular metabolism and preserves intracellular equilibrium. In ocular biology, autophagic activity is involved in structural morphogenesis during eye development and becomes dysregulated across a spectrum of vision-threatening disorders. This review synthesises current evidence on autophagy throughout distinct ocular compartments, with particular attention given to its pathogenic contributions to corneal disease, cataract formation, glaucomatous neurodegeneration, and major retinopathies, with the goal of advancing the understanding of the underlying mechanism in this evolving field.
